title: Gridded ion thruster accelerator grid erosion lifetime
bottleneck: In gridded ion thrusters, electrostatic grids accelerate xenon ions to exhaust velocities up to 100 km/s — but stray ions also bombard the grids, eroding them until efficiency degrades and the engine fails. JPL's NSTAR work traced accelerated wear to nonuniform ion-current density peaked on the thruster centerline (peak-to-average 2:1, peak-to-edge over 10:1). Smoothing the plasma profile halved peak erosion and doubled thruster life, yet erosion remains the fundamental lifetime ceiling.
why_it_blocks: Ion thrusters are the workhorse for deep-space science missions; designers must plan around a hard wear-out limit, constraining burn duration, trajectory options, and redundancy mass.
current_state: NASA demonstrated 48,000+ hours (5.5 years) continuous operation on the NEXT thruster. Xenon replaced corrosive mercury and caesium propellants, and grid materials and magnetic shaping keep improving, but no grid lasts indefinitely.
